title: The diamond
description:
A `Copier` is both a `Scanner` and a `Printer`, and each of those is a `PoweredDevice`. With ordinary inheritance a copier ends up containing **two** separate `PoweredDevice` parts: two power cables.

```
      PoweredDevice
       /         \
   Scanner     Printer
       \         /
         Copier
```

Fix the hierarchy with **virtual inheritance** so there is one shared `PoweredDevice`:

1. `Scanner` and `Printer` inherit from it with `virtual public PoweredDevice`.
2. With virtual inheritance, the *most derived* class constructs the shared base, so `Copier`'s constructor must call `PoweredDevice{ watts }` itself.

The counter `g_devicesBuilt` shows how many `PoweredDevice` parts get constructed.
lessonTitle: Multiple Inheritance and Virtual Base Classes
